newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt sells Alexandria Flour Mills stake. [CORRECTED 17:02 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Egypt sells Alexandria Flour Mills stake. [CORRECTED 17:02 GMT]

text.p: The Egyptian state sold on Thursday 1.176 million shares equivalent to 29.4 percent in Alexandria Flour Mills as part of its privatisation-led economic reform programme, the Capital Market Authority (CMA) said.
The CMA said in a faxed statement the shares were sold for a total 97.02 million pounds, or 82.5 pounds per share.
The state had offered investors 30 percent or 1.2 million shares of Alexandria Flour Mill's total four million shares at an initial price of 75 pounds per share.
The state also sold an additional 10 percent to the miller's workers.
Officials at the Commercial International Investment Company (CIIC), one of the agents for the sale, said the offer had been almost 20 (corrects from 24) times oversubscribed.
They said they did not know why the remaining 24,000 shares were not sold on Thursday and they expected the state to sell them on Sunday.
London-based brokers T. Hoare and Co. said the stock was the best-valued in the milling sector, one of the most popular on the bourse.
